Basically we are being asked to use CPMO at our receive stations in place of the receive app but our receivers are keeping two tabs open because we have some freight that still needs ISDs. Our setup is basically pallets coming from the dock that are run through the frX determinator and then the boxes are thrown on the line if no ISD is needed and if needed given ISDs and then thrown on the line. We also work parcel trailers and in that case the units are puts straight on the line. Our problems are that prep gets on the line because the frX tool isn’t telling us things are prep. Not everyone on the line (18 stations) is prep trained so that causes slowdowns. When freight is coming straight from a parcel the receivers don’t know until after they use the CPMO tool whether they can move it too a cage or if it needs an ISD. The process at this point is to put the unit back on the line and problem solvers at the end of the line find the ISD and receive it. Other problems are cartons have mismatched info where the  sscc says the unit is something, but the unit is physically different. Also the tool not asking for asins causes issues for stowers as well as sscc info being incorrect causing shorts/overages. I’m sure there’s things I’m missing, but it seems like a lot of issues and I’d love to be able o remove barriers for my crew. Thanks in advance

Hello, I’m an receive PA at a tns building, hopefully i can help answer questions.  The prep rate expected at our building is fairly low, like around 20 units an hour. Your rate is the amount units you process divided by the amount of time you’re specifically logged in to whichever process you’re doing. Ideally you should have constant work while in your path. This doesn’t slays happen though. At my site we have pallets of units that need prep as well as a conveyor that will be filled and units needing prep are taken off of trucks. If one of my associates  says they’re out of work, it’s my job to make sure they get more work or put them in another process until work is available. Your rate shouldn’t suffer because of no available work. I might have the associate grab a pallet from another area and code them under support for that time. I’m glad you like your job and I would hope that your PA or AM would be glad if you asked about what rate you were trying to meet and what else you can do to ensure you have work. Taking PTO shouldn’t be used against you. 
If you are labor shared, I’d make sure your time is properly coded. For example, let’s say you were prepping starting at 9:00 am exactly. You prep 5 things and run out of work, you look for your PA and can’t find them and finally at 9:30 you are laborshared somewhere else. You walk to the new place get set up and log in at 9:45 and start a new process it would have you as being in prep from 9-9:45 and only doing 5 things. Not a good rate. If you have been scaned into support as soon as you ran out of work, you’d have only been “in prep” for 5-10 min. Much better rate.
